transcript:
This message comes from Capital One with the Capital One Saver Card.
Earn unlimited 3% cash back on dining and entertainment.
Capital One. What's in your wallet? Terms apply. Details at CapitalOne.com.
This is NPR News Now. The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh. The Fort Hood shooter's execution in December
won't be live streamed after all. Today, President Trump announced on social media
he canceled those plans. Trump reversed course after Defense Secretary Pete
Hexeth elicited strong opposition from Democrats and Republicans. Vice President J.D. Vance was
among those who said he would not watch Nidal Hassan's execution. The Republican Party is
facing the prospect of losing control of Congress in the November midterm elections.
At a White House rose garden event a short time ago, President Trump checked off
a long list of states where he has campaigned for Republican candidates in recent weeks.
And we got a lot of them left. We have sort of averaging about one and a half a day.
The Pew Research Center survey conducted this fall reveals many voters are worried about prices and
affordability. 70% of U.S. adults say they've cut back on spending for extras such as eating
out or streaming services. 54% say they have not been able to save money for the future.
The FBI and the U.S. Postal Inspection Service are looking into a series of suspicious mailings
sent to election offices in some states. And Piers Hansi Lo Wang reports officials say some
of the mailings contained a powdery white substance. It's not clear who sent the mail
to election officials in states including Louisiana, Ohio and Oklahoma. Deputy Chief
Inspector Brendan Donohue says the U.S. Postal Inspection Service was able to stop the delivery
of at least one of the mailings. Some of the letters have contained an unknown substance and
we're working closely with our law enforcement partners to respond to each incident. With less
than three weeks until November 3rd, voting officials around the country are working to
carry out the midterm elections. And the investigation has not stopped early voting.
In a statement, the National Association of Secretaries of State and the National Association
of State Election Directors say, "Those who administer our election should never fear for
their safety while carrying out their essential duties." Hansi Lo Wang, NPR News.
Israel says commercial goods have not entered Gaza for the last several days.
It's blaming Hamas for imposing high taxes on Palestinian merchants and Piers Danielestron
has more. Israel says merchants in Gaza refused to import goods because Hamas imposed high taxes
and threatened merchants. Hamas called it a voluntary payment. Because of the crisis,
commercial goods did not enter Gaza over the last two days, cutting off about 50 percent
of all shipments of essential items to Gaza. Market prices in Gaza have skyrocketed.
Shana Lo of the Norwegian Refugee Council Aid Group.
Any disruption to the flow of goods, whether they're humanitarian or commercial,
is a shock to the system in Gaza.
In Gaza, a Palestinian trucker's union blamed Israel for halting the shipments.
Gaza's two million people face a humanitarian crisis with Israeli restrictions on aid supplies.
That's Danielestron. It's NPR.
The Irish novelist Sally Rooney and her publisher say her books will no longer be sold in Britain
because of her support for a pro-Palestinian group the British government has banned.
Rooney is a longtime supporter of Palestinian causes.
And Piers Lauren Freire has the latest from London.
Sally Rooney has said she'll donate book profits to Palestine Action, a protest group the British
government has labeled a terror organization that makes it illegal to voice or give any support to
the group. Rooney's publisher says the label also means that it can't send Rooney her British
earnings. And that, it says, is a, quote, unconscionable situation for a publisher.
Rooney says she is in full agreement to stop British sales of her books, which include normal
people and conversations with friends, both of which have also been adapted for TV.
Rooney says she's been honest about her beliefs and is, quote, wholly prepared
to accept the consequences. Lauren Freire, NPR News, London.
In the US, businesses are paying higher prices before products reach the store shelves. Some of
those costs could be passed along to customers. The Labor Department reports wholesale prices
were 6.3% higher in September than they were the year before. Gasoline and diesel prices have been
surging, a result of the US war with Iran, although President Trump has pinned the diesel
price hike on Ukraine's attacks on Russia oil refineries. By the way, Ukraine has
resumed its attacks on Russia's oil facilities. The cost of diesel has become a political
liability for President Trump and the GOP ahead of the midterms. I'm Lakshmi Singh, NPR News.

topics.text: Trump cancels plan to livestream Nidal Hasan's execution after bipartisan opposition
Republicans face possible loss of Congress in November midterms; Trump touts campaign stops
Pew survey finds Americans cutting back on dining out and streaming, unable to save
FBI and Postal Inspection Service probe suspicious powdery mailings to election offices in several states
Israel says no commercial goods entered Gaza for two days, blames Hamas taxes on merchants
Irish novelist Sally Rooney halts British book sales over support for banned group Palestine Action
Wholesale prices rose 6.3% in September year over year, driven by gas and diesel costs
